title: François Jacob discovered with Jacques Monod how the cell switches genes on and off, and won the Nobel Prize

trailer.text: François Jacob was a French biologist and a laureate of the 1965 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.
According to the Collège de France, his parents both came from Jewish families, and his grandfather Albert Franck was the first Jew to reach the rank of Lieutenant General.
In 1940 he left his medical studies and joined the Free French Forces in London, and because of his war injuries he was unable to practise surgery.
In 1950 he joined the Institut Pasteur, where, with Jacques Monod and their colleagues, he discovered that some genes control the activity of other genes.
Jacob and Monod called such an arrangement an operon, and in 1965 they won the Nobel Prize together with André Lwoff.

paragraphs.text: François Jacob was born in June 1920 in Nancy, France, the only son of Simon Jacob and Thérèse Franck.
According to the Collège de France, both his parents came from Jewish families.
His maternal grandfather, Albert Franck, was the first Jew to reach the rank of Lieutenant General.
According to the Embryo Project Encyclopedia, Jacob said that he became an atheist after his bar mitzvah.
He began studying medicine in Paris, with the intention of becoming a surgeon.
On 2 June 1940 his mother died of Hodgkin's disease.
In June 1940, in his second year of medical studies, Jacob left France and joined the Free French Forces in London.
He refused to accept the French surrender and joined General de Gaulle, and so his plan to become a surgeon was interrupted.
He was sent to Africa as a medical officer and took part in the fighting in Fezzan, Libya, Tripolitania and Tunisia, where he was wounded.
According to President Hollande's speech, on 10 May 1943 his body was hit by mortar fragments in the sands of Tunisia.
In August 1944, while in the Second Armoured Division, Jacob was severely wounded in Normandy.
He recounted that his entire right side was filled with grenade fragments, and described it as a dreadful time.
He remained in hospital for seven months, and was awarded the Croix de la Libération, the highest French military decoration of the war.

stations.title: The long road to the laboratory

paragraphs.text: Because of his injuries Jacob was unable to practise surgery, and he worked in various fields before turning to biology.
After the war he worked at the Cabanel Center, a former gunpowder factory converted into an antibiotics factory.
In 1947 he married a pianist from the Bloch family, and they had four children.
André Lwoff turned him down again and again, and finally accepted him into his laboratory.
In 1950 Jacob joined the Institut Pasteur, already in his thirties.
According to NPR, the laboratory was in an attic, was cramped, and its equipment was old.
Jacob began working with Elie Wollman.
Together they discovered that conjugation could be used to map genes in bacteria.
Working with Wollman, Jacob showed that prophages insert their genes into the DNA of the host bacterium.

stations.title: The question: when is a gene silent and when is it active

paragraphs.text: No one at the time offered a good explanation of how genes in the bacterium E. coli or in its prophages could be quiet one moment and active the next.
Many scientists assumed that cells constantly produce a steady supply of all their proteins.
Jacques Monod found that only after the bacteria had eaten all the glucose did they begin to produce beta-galactosidase in significant amounts.
In 1958 Jacob and Monod began to collaborate.
They and their colleagues at the Institut Pasteur isolated mutant E. coli bacteria that failed to eat lactose in interesting ways.
The strangest mutants produced beta-galactosidase and permease all the time, even when there was no lactose to digest.
The PaJaMo experiment was designed to analyse the roles of the gene products of the bacterium's lactose degradation system.
Its results overturned established ideas, and explained enzymatic induction by a mechanism based on repression.
The discovery revealed two types of gene: some encode structural proteins, and some control the expression of the former.

stations.title: An evening at the cinema, July 1958

paragraphs.text: One day in July 1958, Jacob squirmed in his seat in a Paris movie theater.
According to the Collège de France, he then realised that his two experimental systems, lysogeny and the lactose system, were part of the same molecular mechanism.
According to National Geographic, he then caught a glimpse of how genes work together to make life possible.
When he tried to sketch out his ideas for his wife, he was disappointed.
National Geographic and the Collège de France: Jacob

stations.title: The operon: a switch for genes

paragraphs.text: According to National Geographic, the repressor is a protein that blocks the production of proteins from the gene for beta-galactosidase and from other genes involved in feeding on lactose.
When lactose is present, the repressor detaches from the gene, and the gene is activated.
Jacob and Monod called such an arrangement of structural and regulatory genes an operon.
They also proposed the existence of messenger RNA, a partial copy of the DNA that carries genetic information to the rest of the cell.
At a meeting of Jacob, Brenner and Crick, Crick concluded that the unstable substance X could only be RNA.
According to the Collège de France, the model was completed on Christmas Eve 1960, ten years after Jacob joined Lwoff's laboratory.
According to the same source, their joint work was published in 1961, and showed that gene activity is finely tuned to the needs of the cell.
They demonstrated the existence and coordinated action of regulatory sequences, repressors and messenger RNA.
From then on, the genome was viewed not merely as a collection of genes, but as a set of regulated and coordinated programs.
According to Carl Zimmer, all the cells in the body have the same DNA, and yet they are very different from one another.
According to Zimmer, if you cannot turn genes on and off, you die.
The discovery was a conceptual breakthrough that had not been predicted, seven years after the elucidation of the structure of DNA.
According to a memorial article at Northwestern, Jacob and Monod were the first to propose a general model explaining how genes are used and regulated in protein synthesis.
According to President Hollande, this was the first time a model for representing genes had been defined.
According to the Institut Pasteur, the development of the operon model had a major impact on biology as a whole.
In 1962 Jacob received the Charles Léopold Mayer Prize of the Academy of Sciences.
According to Nobel sources, in 1964 he was appointed Professor at the Collège de France, where a chair of Cell Genetics was created for him.
In December 1965 the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine was awarded jointly to Jacob, Lwoff and Monod.
According to President Hollande, Jacob was then 45 years old.
Jacob was a member of the Académie des Sciences, Paris, from 1977 and of the Académie Française from 1996.
The universities that awarded him honorary degrees include the Weizmann Institute of Science.
He also received the Lewis Thomas Prize for Writing about Science.
On 14 November 2012 a new building bearing his name was inaugurated at the Institut Pasteur.
According to Rockefeller University, the selection committee of the Lewis Thomas Prize chose Jacob for the 1994 prize.
In 1963 Jacob, together with Sydney Brenner, proposed the replicon hypothesis.

In the late 1960s he left bacteria for mice, and the teratocarcinoma cells studied in his laboratory are the ancestors of the stem cells that are now grown in hundreds of laboratories across the world.
To move to the study of embryonic development, he gave up his precious collection, which numbered hundreds of E. coli mutants.
The change from the fast tempo of bacterial genetics to the slow tempo of mouse genetics was a tough test.
He proposed creating a mouse institute, and the idea was warmly welcomed, but the project never came to fruition.
In 1970 he published "The Logic of Life", a history of heredity that established him as a leading historian of science.
He argued that evolution is more akin to tinkering (bricolage) than to engineering.
According to the Institut Pasteur, throughout his life he was committed to combating racism and preventing the misuse of genetic information.
According to President Hollande, he was a member of the National Ethics Council and was concerned about the possible abuses of genetic manipulation.
According to a memorial article at Northwestern, it is sometimes said that Monod was the great theoretician and Jacob the superb experimentalist.
According to the same article, many times it was Jacob who anticipated the mechanism, proposed it and convinced Monod to accept it.
According to the Collège de France, Jacob and Monod grew apart, and neither was enthusiastic about the other's writings.
According to Encyclopaedia Britannica, Jacob died on 19 April 2013 in Paris.
According to President Hollande, he was a great and exceptional man who gave France many reasons to believe in itself.

claims.text: לפי מכון פסטר, לפיתוח מודל האופרון הייתה השפעה מרכזית על הביולוגיה כולה.
claims.quote: The development of the operon model had a major impact on biology as a whole

claims.text: ב-1962 קיבל ז'קוב את פרס שארל לאופולד מאייר של האקדמיה למדעים.
claims.quote: 1962: Charles Léopold Mayer Prize from the Academy of Sciences

claims.text: לפי מקורות הנובל, ב-1964 מונה ז'קוב לפרופסור בקולז' דה פרנס, שם הוקמה עבורו קתדרה לגנטיקה של התא.
claims.quote: In 1964 he was appointed Professor at the Collège de France, where a chair of Cell Genetics was created for him.

claims.text: בדצמבר 1965 הוענק פרס נובל לז'קוב, ללבוף ולמונו.
claims.quote: In December 1965, the Nobel Prize for Physiology or Medicine was awarded to François Jacob, André Lwoff and Jacques Monod

claims.text: לפי הנשיא הולנד, ז'קוב קיבל את פרס נובל ב-1965 בגיל 45.
claims.quote: Cest avec André LWOFF et Jacques MONOD que François JACOB reçut, en 1965 il avait 45 ans la plus haute de toutes les distinctions

claims.text: ז'קוב חבר באקדמיה למדעים של פריז (1977) ובאקדמיה הצרפתית (1996).
claims.quote: François Jacob is a member of the Académie des Sciences, Paris (1977) and of the Académie Française, Paris (1996).

claims.text: לפי מאמר זיכרון בנורת'ווסטרן, ז'קוב קיבל את פרס לואיס תומאס לכתיבה על מדע ב-1996.
claims.quote: He also received the Lewis Thomas Prize for Writing about Science (1996)

claims.text: ב-14 בנובמבר 2012 נחנך במכון פסטר בניין חדש הנושא את שמו של ז'קוב.
claims.quote: On November 14, 2012, alongside the President of the Republic, he was delighted to be able to inaugurate the new building that bears his name.

claims.text: ב-1963, יחד עם סידני ברנר, הציע ז'קוב את השערת הרפליקון.
claims.quote: Together with Sydney Brenner, he proposed the replicon hypothesis in 1963

claims.text: בסוף שנות ה-60 עזב ז'קוב את החיידקים לטובת עכברים, ובמעבדתו נחקרו תאי טרטוקרצינומה, אבות תאי הגזע.
claims.quote: the teratocarcinoma cells studied in his laboratory are the ancestors of the stem cells that are now grown in hundreds of laboratories across the world.

claims.text: כדי לעבור לחקר התפתחות העובר ויתר ז'קוב על אוסף ענק של מוטנטים של E. coli.
claims.quote: he gave up his precious collection of hundreds ofEscherichia colibacterial mutants

claims.text: המעבר מהקצב המהיר של גנטיקת חיידקים לקצב האיטי של גנטיקת העכבר היה מבחן קשה.
claims.quote: the change in tempo of the experiments, from the presto of bacterial genetics to the adagio of mouse genetics, was a tough test

claims.text: ז'קוב הציע להקים מכון לעכברים; הרעיון התקבל בחום אך הפרויקט לא יצא לפועל.
claims.quote: François Jacob proposed the creation of a mouse institute, an idea that was warmly welcomed by his fellow biologists. The project never saw the light of day.

claims.text: ב-1970 פרסם ז'קוב את "ההיגיון של החיים", היסטוריה של התורשה שביססה אותו כהיסטוריון מדע מוביל.
claims.quote: In 1970, he published La Logique du vivant (The Logic of Life), a history of heredity that immediately established him as a leading historian of science

claims.text: ז'קוב טען שהאבולוציה דומה יותר לטלאי-עבודה (bricolage) מאשר להנדסה.
claims.quote: Jacob argued that the process of evolution by natural selection is more akin to bricolage (tinkering) than to engineering

claims.text: ז'קוב הקדיש את חייו למאבק בגזענות ובשימוש לרעה במידע גנטי.
claims.quote: his lifelong commitment to combating racism and preventing the misuse of genetic information

claims.text: לפי הנשיא הולנד, ז'קוב היה חבר במועצה האתית הלאומית ודאג מהסטיות האפשריות של מניפולציות גנטיות.
claims.quote: Membre du Conseil consultatif national déthique, il salarmait des dérives possibles des manipulations génétiques.

claims.text: לפי מאמר זיכרון בנורת'ווסטרן, אומרים לעיתים שמונו היה התאורטיקן הגדול וז'קוב הניסיין המעולה.
claims.quote: Despite sometimes it has been said that Monod was the great theoretician and Jacob the fantastic experimentalist

claims.text: לפי אותו מאמר, פעמים רבות היה זה ז'קוב שצפה את המנגנון, הציע אותו ושכנע את מונו לקבלו.
claims.quote: Many times it was Jacob who anticipated the mechanism, proposed it and convinced Monod to eventually accept his ideas.

claims.text: לפי הכולז' דה פרנס, ז'קוב ומונו התרחקו זה מזה, ואיש מהם לא התלהב מכתביו של האחר.
claims.quote: The Jacques-François duo grew apart. Each was less than enthusiastic about the other's writings.

claims.text: לפי הנשיא הולנד, ז'קוב היה אדם גדול ויוצא דופן שנתן לצרפת סיבות רבות להאמין בעצמה.
claims.quote: François JACOB était un grand homme, un homme exceptionnel qui a donné à notre pays tant de raisons de croire en lui-même.

claims.text: לפי נאום הנשיא הולנד, ב-8 באוגוסט 1944 נפצע ז'קוב מעשרות רסיסי רימון.
claims.quote: Puis un an plus tard, le 8 août 1944, par des dizaines déclats de grenade : il allait en souffrir toute sa vie.

claims.text: לפי הכולז' דה פרנס, ב-1 באוגוסט נחת ז'קוב בחוף יוטה שבנורמנדי, ושמונה ימים לאחר מכן נפצע קשה בהתקפה אווירית.
claims.quote: On August 1st, he landed on Utah Beach in Normandy. Eight days later, he was seriously wounded in an air attack.

claims.text: לפי הכולז' דה פרנס, ז'קוב נעשה פרופסור בקולז' דה פרנס חצי שנה לפני פרס הנובל בדצמבר 1965.
claims.quote: Six months earlier, François Jacob had become Professor of Cell Genetics at the Collège de France.

claims.text: לפי אוניברסיטת רוקפלר, ועדת הבחירה של פרס לואיס תומאס בחרה בז'קוב לפרס של שנת 1994.
claims.quote: He was also a member of the Selection Committee that chose Dr. Jacob for 1994.

claims.text: הוא קיבל גם את פרס לואיס תומאס לכתיבה על מדע.
claims.quote: with the second Lewis Thomas Prize on Wednesday, May 25.
